calls.head: Colorado shoots far more than St. Louis
calls.body: Colorado ranks 1st of 32 for shot volume, toward the relentless end; St. Louis ranks 23rd, toward the selective end.
calls.call: Colorado takes more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than St. Louis.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Colorado had 74.6 per 60 and St. Louis 56.4 per 60. Coming in, Colorado was at 68.4 per 60 and St. Louis at 53.7 per 60.

calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, St. Louis sits 10th of 32, at the deep end of the scale. Colorado is 32nd, at the top-heavy end.
calls.call: St. Louis spreads its forward ice time deeper down the lineup than Colorado.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, St. Louis had 46% and Colorado 40%. Coming in, St. Louis was at 43% and Colorado at 39%.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 73% chance, and Colorado delivered.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis only a 27% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: St. Louis was kept to the outside
surprises.body: St. Louis needed 19.7 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 14.4 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: St. Louis tried a different line
surprises.body: D. Dube, P. Suter, Z. Dean played 10:26 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of St. Louis’s usual lines.
